turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith stops just inside the door. She's still in her office clothes, laptop bag on one shoulder. She doesn't sit. She looks at the desk, then at you.*

Mr. or Ms. Hale. I have until 4:40.

Owen found out about this zero from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me first.

So I'll start there. Who decided to give him the zero, and when?
Okay. Let's look at the essay.

*She sets her bag down, finally, and takes the chair across from you. She doesn't take her coat off.*

Okay.

Before you open it, I want to know what's on this desk. The essay, yes. The checker report, with a date on it? The school's academic integrity policy? Anything Owen wrote or said before the zero went in?

*She takes a legal pad out of the bag and uncaps a pen.*

I'm writing down what you put in front of me. Start with the report. Which software, what version, and what exactly does it say?
You're very sharp, you know that?

*She doesn't look up from the pad.*

It's not a compliment I need.

*A beat. The pen stops.*

Are you trying to settle me down, or are you stalling? Either way, the report. Which software, what date was it run, and who ran it?
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.

*Now she looks up.*

"The timestamp issue."

I asked whether the report had a date on it. I didn't say there was a problem with one.

*She puts the pen down on the pad.*

So what is the timestamp issue? Don't tell me I caught it. Tell me what it is. I'm writing it down.
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.

*She doesn't move. Her voice stays level.*

"Had to flag it."

Under which rule? Which section of the policy says you had to, and was Owen heard before the zero went in?

*She taps the pad once.*

You also didn't answer my question about the timestamp. I asked twice. I'm noting that.

I'm not here to be agreed with, and I'm not here to see your side yet. Show me the report.
